title: Microservice SDK Samples: Stream/Retry Adapters + CLI & Server Templates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a set of compact, production-minded SDK example templates that demonstrate streaming ergonomics and robust retry/adapters across Next.js (SSR + Edge), FastAPI, Go net/http, and a CLI tailing tool. Focus on patterns teams can copy: safe reconnection, idempotent retries, progressive output buffering, graceful cancellation, and token-level cost visibility. Deliverables: four runnable templates, CI tests that simulate transient failures and resume, README + migration notes for teams upgrading from naive streaming loops.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example: supports server-side streaming and client hydration via EventSource/Fetch + resume token; README with 1-min quickstart
FastAPI example: async endpoint that proxies streaming responses, backpressure-friendly using asyncio streams; integration test simulates downstream timeouts and confirms retry logic
Go example: idiomatic net/http server showing streaming handler with context cancellation and reconnect semantics; includes small client demonstrating exponential backoff with jitter
CLI example: cross-language pattern (TS/Go) that tails and retries a streaming response, exposes --resume and --checkpoint flags
Each example includes unit or integration tests in CI that inject transient errors and verify that output resumes without duplication more than once per token window
All code follows SDK flavor: uses official Python/TS/Go SDKs and demonstrates recommended retry config values and streaming APIs
README migration notes explaining trade-offs vs naive read-loop approaches and recommended SLOs/observability signals to track

notes: Design trade-off: prefer resume tokens at message/chunk boundary instead of byte offsets to avoid partial-token duplication across different model codecs
We initially considered using a shared websocket helper; decided against for simplicity and broadest hosting compatibility (Edge + serverless)
Retries should be idempotent at request level when possible; we recommend a short-lived server-side cache keyed by (request-id, resume-token) to avoid re-processing expensive prompts
Cost visibility: provide token counters at client-side per-session; recommend emitting periodic cost checkpoints to the Console
Security: examples will not include tenant secrets — use environment variables and demonstrate KMS-wrapped keys in docs separately

Provide a helper library snippet for resume token serialization and checksum verification
